advices.diagnosis: The class exhibits low cohesion (LCOM4=2) because its methods operate on two distinct sets of attributes: `title` and `describe_customer` rely on `self._width`, while `order_count` and `mail_summary` rely on `self._repository` and `self._mailer`. Additionally, `describe_customer` demonstrates feature envy by accessing four attributes of the `Customer` object, suggesting that the formatting logic belongs closer to the data source or a dedicated formatter, rather than in the view which only holds a width constraint.

suggestions.title: Extract customer formatting logic
suggestions.sketch: Move the logic in `describe_customer` to a method on the `Customer` class (e.g., `Customer.format_for_report(width)`) or a dedicated `CustomerFormatter` class. This removes the dependency of `ReportView` on the internal structure of `Customer` and isolates the `self._width` usage. If moved to `Customer`, `ReportView` simply calls `customer.format_for_report(self._width)`. This reduces the attribute coupling within `ReportView` by removing the need for `ReportView` to know how to assemble customer parts, potentially allowing `describe_customer` to be removed or simplified to a pure delegation, which helps consolidate the method-attribute graph.

suggestions.title: Separate reporting and notification responsibilities
suggestions.sketch: Split `ReportView` into two classes: `ReportFormatter` (handling `title`, `describe_customer`, and `self._width`) and `ReportNotifier` (handling `mail_summary` and `order_count`, depending on `repository` and `mailer`). This eliminates the LCOM4 warning by ensuring each new class has a single cohesive set of attributes. `ReportFormatter` would have DCC=0 (or 1 if it references Customer), and `ReportNotifier` would have DCC=2 (Repository, Mailer). This adheres to the Single Responsibility Principle.

advices.risk_notes: Splitting the class increases the number of classes in the system and may require updating the composition root where `ReportView` is instantiated. Moving logic to `Customer` requires ensuring `Customer` is not a simple data transfer object (DTO) if the project architecture forbids behavior on DTOs. The `mail_summary` method currently returns a dict from the mailer; if this return value is used for UI feedback, separating it from the view might require a new interface or event mechanism.
